headline_marked: Apple unveils [[M6 and M5 Ultra chips]] with 2nm process and quad-die architecture
headline: Apple unveils M6 and M5 Ultra chips with 2nm process and quad-die architecture
summary: Apple's new M6 chip is built on a 2nm process with a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, while the M5 Ultra features a quad-die architecture for extreme performance.
details: Apple has announced its latest M6 and M5 Ultra chips, marking a significant leap in performance and AI capabilities. The M6 chip, built on a cutting-edge 2-nanometer process, boasts a 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, delivering enhanced speed and power efficiency for everyday tasks and creative projects.

The M5 Ultra chip represents Apple's most powerful offering to date, utilizing a quad-die architecture for professional and AI workloads. It features an impressive up-to-36-core CPU and up-to-80-core GPU, supported by a massive 1.2TB/s of unified memory bandwidth, a 50% increase over the M3 Ultra.

The M6 chip's CPU complex includes 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores, offering the world's fastest single-threaded performance and up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance compared to its predecessor. Its 12-core GPU includes a Neural Accelerator in each core, providing nearly 30% more peak GPU compute for AI tasks.

With up to 2x the peak compute of previous generations, the Dual 16-core Neural Engine in the M6 chip significantly accelerates on-device AI workflows. The M5 Ultra, designed for ultimate desktop performance, pushes the boundaries for running massive AI models and complex computational tasks.

These new chips are integrated into Apple's latest hardware, with the M6 powering the new Mac mini and the M5 Ultra featured in the new Mac Studio. This release underscores Apple's commitment to advancing silicon technology for both consumer and professional markets.
